Hosting playbook

Eurovision night — host the perfect watch party

Eurovision night is the annual living-room ritual where you watch the Eurovision Song Contest with friends, rate every song, and argue about which country deserves to win. This guide turns it from passive viewing into a competitive, scored party game using Eurovision Games — a free browser-based companion that handles predictions, trivia, and scoring while you watch.

What is Eurovision night?

Eurovision night is the live grand-final broadcast of the Eurovision Song Contest, held on the second Saturday of May each year. In 2026 the grand final airs on Saturday 16 May 2026 from Vienna, with semi-finals earlier that week. Across Europe (and Australia) it is a single televised live event watched by ~160 million people; in homes it has become a competitive social event, a costume party, and a drinking game all at once.

How to host (10-step playbook)

  1. 1. Pick a venue. Living-room, garden, projector on a wall — or a Zoom/FaceTime call if you're scattered.
  2. 2. Confirm the broadcast. National broadcaster (BBC One, ARD, ERT, RAI, etc.) or the official YouTube live-stream where licensing allows.
  3. 3. Send a save-the-date. Doors open ~1 hour before kick-off so guests can settle and lock predictions.
  4. 4. Open Eurovision Games. Create a room at eurovision.games on the host's phone or laptop, share the join link.
  5. 5. Set the lineup. Print or screenshot the 2026 running order so everyone has a reference for predictions.
  6. 6. Lock predictions. Before the first song, every guest picks Top 5 and Worst 5.
  7. 7. Watch song-by-song. React, score, take photos. Encourage opinionated commentary.
  8. 8. Use breaks for trivia duels. The interval act is ~25 minutes — perfect duel window.
  9. 9. Watch the vote. Jury vote first, then televote — the most chaotic 25 minutes of TV all year.
  10. 10. Crown winners. After the televote, the app reveals five trophy cards — Champion, Thief, Duelist, Oracle, Guru.

Food and drink ideas

The classic move: one snack per favourite country. Sweden = meatballs and Daim. Italy = arancini. Greece = souvlaki. UK = sausage rolls. Don't over-cater — the focus is the screen. A flexible buffet that survives the 4-hour run-time beats a hot served dinner. Mocktails travel well; an alcohol-free option keeps drivers and non-drinkers happy through to the televote.

Time-zone tips

Grand final start times vary by country: 21:00 CET (Germany, France, Spain), 20:00 BST/UTC+1 (UK, Ireland), 22:00 EET (Greece, Cyprus, Finland, Israel), 05:00 AEDT next morning (Australia — record it). If you're hosting cross-country, align on the host's local kick-off and start the room 30 minutes earlier.

Game options inside the room

  • Predictions: Top 5, Worst 5 — locked before the show, scored automatically against jury + televote.
  • Trivia duels: Head-to-head between any two players. Winner steals points from loser. Default per-pair cap of 3 duels (rematches counted) prevents grinding one opponent.
  • Quiz rounds: Fast-fire rounds the host triggers between performances.
  • Sudden-death tiebreak: Optional. If players tie a winner category, the room votes — Accept (share the trophy) or Sudden Death. If Sudden Death wins, the tied players fight through a 3-question trivia match.
